memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I will heap calamities on them and spend my arrows against them. I will send wasting famine against them, consuming pestilence and deadly plague; I will send against them the fangs of wild beasts, the venom of vipers that glide in the dust. In the street the sword will make them childless; in their homes terror will reign.'" — Deut 32:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are among the darkest verses in the song, describing the calamities that would follow persistent rebellion. We do not read them with cold detachment, nor do we soften them. They picture the full weight of what it means for a people to be handed over to the consequences of forsaking the God who protected them. When His shielding presence is withdrawn, the world becomes a dangerous and terrifying place.

There is a hard but important truth beneath these images: God's protection is a mercy we too easily take for granted. So much of the danger and evil in the world is held back by God's restraining hand. When people persistently reject Him and He withdraws that protecting hand, the true horror of a world in rebellion is exposed. Sin, left to run its course, brings ruin.

This should not lead us to fear, but to gratitude and humble dependence. Every day of safety, every mercy, every good thing we enjoy is a gift of God's protecting grace, not something we have earned or can take for granted.

And these dark verses make us long all the more for the Saviour. Into a world under the shadow of sin's consequences, Jesus came. He faced the full darkness — the terror, the sword, death itself — and passed through it, so that those who trust Him might be brought safely home. The One who could rightly send judgment instead took judgment upon Himself. Where these verses show us what sin deserves, the cross shows us how deeply we are loved.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I recognise and thank God for His daily protecting grace?
2. How does the reality of sin's consequences make me value Christ's rescue more?
3. Am I living in humble dependence on God's mercy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the protecting grace I so easily take for granted. These hard words remind me what sin deserves and how great Your rescue is. Thank You that Christ faced the darkness so I could be brought home. Amen.
